schema.text: DS-GPA predicted median overall survival (less than 6 months vs at least 6 months). Radio-resistant means sarcoma, melanoma, or renal cell carcinoma. Metastasis within 5 mm of one hippocampus (yes or no).

schema.label: Step 1 registration
schema.text: Consenting patients believed to be eligible are registered in OPEN with an abbreviated eligibility checklist. After registration, neurocognitive assessments, quality-of-life questionnaires, and health economics assessments may be administered.

schema.label: Step 2 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Randomize after baseline assessments and before treatment. Stratification factors are collected at registration. Protocol treatment begins within 14 days of enrolment.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy, 30 Gy in 10 fractions, plus memantine. Memantine starts the same day as whole brain radiotherapy and must start no later than before the fourth fraction. The target dose is 20 mg (10 mg twice daily), escalated by 5 mg per week.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Stereotactic radiosurgery in a single fraction: 22 Gy for lesions under 4 cc, and 18 to 20 Gy for lesions of 4 to 10 cc. The schema footnote says further details are in the treatment section.

schema.label: Observation
schema.text: Both arms then enter observation and event monitoring. If brain metastases or systemic disease progress, the patient remains under observation.

eligibility: Five or more brain metastases, counted on a contrast-enhanced T1 MRI obtained within 30 days of randomization. Pathologic diagnosis, cytology or histology, of a non-hematopoietic malignancy.

The largest brain metastasis must be smaller than 2.5 cm in maximal diameter. Total tumor volume must be 30 cm3 or less, estimated as the product of three perpendicular diameters divided by 2, or by direct slice-by-slice contouring.

The centre must be able to treat with Gamma Knife, Cyberknife, or a linear accelerator radiosurgery system, or must have access to an open centre that can. The enrolling facility must be IROC-credentialed for stereotactic radiosurgery and hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy, or have access to a credentialed centre where the study is open. Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0, 1, or 2.

Able and willing to complete quality-of-life questionnaires in English or French, alone or with assistance, before randomization. Creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min within 28 days before registration. Section 4 does not list other numeric hematology or chemistry floors.

Pregnant or nursing women are excluded. Men or women of childbearing potential who will not use adequate contraception are excluded.

Inability to complete a brain MRI, and known allergy to gadolinium, are exclusions. Prior cranial radiation is excluded. Planned cytotoxic chemotherapy within 48 hours before or after stereotactic radiosurgery or hippocampal-avoidant whole brain radiotherapy is excluded.

Primary germ cell tumor, small cell carcinoma, and lymphoma are excluded. Widespread definitive leptomeningeal metastasis is excluded, including cranial nerve palsy, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, ependymal involvement, cranial nerve involvement on imaging, suspicious linear meningeal enhancement, or cerebrospinal fluid positive for tumor cells.
A brain metastasis within 5 mm of the optic chiasm or either optic nerve is excluded. Prior surgical resection of a brain metastasis is excluded. Stereotactic biopsies are allowed.

Prior allergic reaction to memantine, or hypersensitivity to any memantine excipient, is excluded. Current alcohol or drug abuse is excluded. Current use of NMDA antagonists such as amantadine, ketamine, or dextromethorphan is excluded.

Chronic liver disease or cirrhosis, for example Child-Pugh class B or C, is excluded. Clinically significant untreated or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions, and symptomatic cardiac dysfunction, are excluded, including unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous year, ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication, second or third degree atrioventricular block, and uncontrolled hypertension.
Current active or uncontrolled urinary tract infection is excluded. A history of epilepsy or seizures in a patient not currently taking anti-epileptic medication is excluded.

Any other serious illness that the local investigator judges would compromise safety, preclude the planned treatment, or prevent protocol management is excluded. Architectural distortion of the lateral ventricles that, in the local investigator's opinion, makes hippocampal delineation challenging is excluded.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: International multicenter open-label randomized phase II trial of limited-dose 177Lu-DOTATATE compared with everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only) in metastatic or unresectable well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with a prior durable response to 177Lu-DOTATATE. Planned sample size is 100 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Longer responders (at least 24 months) vs standard responders (less than 24 months) to initial PRRT. A responder is stable disease, partial response, or complete response per RECIST 1.1. Pancreatic vs extrapancreatic site of origin. Intervening therapy vs no intervening therapy.

schema.label: Randomize 2:1
schema.text: Treatment on either arm continues until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: 177Lu-DOTATATE 7400 MBq (200 mCi) every 8 weeks for 2 cycles.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Everolimus 10 mg daily, or sunitinib 37.5 mg daily, or cabozantinib 60 mg daily. Pancreatic NET may receive everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only). Midgut NET may receive only everolimus or cabozantinib (US patients only).

schema.label: Crossover
schema.text: At objective progression per RECIST 1.1, Arm 2 may cross over to Arm 1. The schema prints the Arm 1 regimen a second time at that step, again 7400 MBq (200 mCi) every 8 weeks for 2 cycles. Crossover is also available to patients who stop everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib for toxicity and later have objective progression, if they stayed in protocol follow-up after stopping the Arm 2 agent chosen at the start of protocol therapy.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Disease status every 12 weeks until objective progression, then telephone, virtual, or clinic survival follow-up every 6 months until death.

eligibility: The study population is metastatic or unresectable well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that progressed no sooner than 12 months after prior peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

Age at least 18. Metastatic, histologically confirmed grade 1 or 2 well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, including an unknown primary thought to be gastroenteropancreatic, using the 7th edition TNM classification.

A positive gallium-68 DOTATATE, copper-64 DOTATATE, or octreotide scan within 12 months is recommended and within 36 months is allowed. A target lesion is positive if its SUVmax is greater than the SUV mean of normal liver.

Prior PRRT must have been 3 or 4 cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE, or a cumulative exposure of 22,200 MBq (600 mCi) or 29,600 MBq (800 mCi), within plus or minus 10 percent, given within a 52-week period. No previous targeted alpha therapy.

Radiologic progression per RECIST 1.1 after prior PRRT, and no sooner than 12 months from the last scan after initial PRRT, during which stable disease, partial response, or complete response was maintained.

Intervening systemic anticancer therapy is allowed if the patient benefited from initial PRRT for at least 12 months and then progressed per RECIST 1.1 on that intervening therapy. A somatostatin analogue given for functional control is not intervening systemic therapy.

If intervening therapy included a VEGF inhibitor, sunitinib cannot be the Arm 2 standard of care. If it included an mTOR inhibitor, everolimus cannot be the Arm 2 standard of care. If the intervening therapy is an alkylating agent, alkylator exposure cannot exceed 12 months. That 12-month limit also applies to alkylator use before PRRT.

Prior ablative liver therapy or bland embolization is allowed if not within 12 weeks of randomization. Prior chemoembolization and radioembolization are not permitted. A lesion treated with ablation, and lesions in a liver lobe treated with embolization, are not target lesions unless they have since progressed.
No ongoing toxicity from prior PRRT that is grade 3 or higher by CTCAE 5.0. ECOG performance status 2 or better.

Organ and marrow function within 28 days before enrollment: hemoglobin at least 80 g/L (8.0 g/dL), absolute neutrophil count at least 1.0 x 10^9/L (1,000/mm3), platelets at least 80 x 10^9/L (80,000/mm3), total bilirubin less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (Gilbert syndrome may be eligible at or below 3.0 times that limit), and creatinine clearance greater than 50 mL/min by 24-hour urine or Cockcroft-Gault.

Prior or current somatostatin analogues are allowed for carcinoid syndrome control and in the Arm 1 retreatment population. Patients randomized to Arm 2 who receive everolimus, sunitinib (pancreatic NET only), or cabozantinib (US patients only) may not continue somatostatin analogues unless they have a functional syndrome.

The patient must have access to everolimus, or to sunitinib for pancreatic NET, or to cabozantinib for US patients. If the site cannot provide that access, the patient is not eligible. Patients must be treated and followed at the participating centre.

People of reproductive potential must use highly effective contraception during protocol treatment and for 7 months after the last dose for females and 4 months after the last dose for males. Men should avoid fathering a child for 4 months after the last 177Lu-DOTATATE dose. A pregnancy test is part of the pre-study evaluation.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. A prior or concurrent malignancy is eligible when its natural history or treatment would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Exclusions: major surgery within 6 weeks of randomization. Known brain metastases, unless treated, stabilized, and off steroids for at least 4 weeks, with a contrast head CT and/or MRI documenting stable disease before enrollment.

The ineligibility list includes uncontrolled congestive heart failure no worse than NYHA class IIB, as defined in Appendix XIII. Inability to swallow oral medications, or gastrointestinal disease that limits absorption of oral agents, is excluded. Any other significant medical or surgical condition that is uncontrolled and may interfere with completing the study is excluded.

Pregnant women are excluded. Breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib (US patients only), and for 2.5 months after the last 177Lu-DOTATATE treatment.

schema.text: Interpretation A hypofractionated schedule of 55 Gy in 20 fractions is non-inferior to 64 Gy in 32 fractions with regard to both invasive locoregional control and toxicity, and is superior with regard to invasive locoregional control. 55 Gy in 20 fractions should be adopted as a standard of care for bladder preservation in patients with locally advanced bladder cancer.

Inclusion and exclusion criteria were similar between the trials ( appendix p 1 ).

followup.window: In BC2001, annual follow-up for disease events (recurrence of local or distant disease) and patient status was prospectively collected up to July 11, 2016.
To account for the difference in length of disease follow-up assessments between trials, the period of observation was set at 5 years.

schema.text: Chemotherapy-naive patients with unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer were randomized 1:1 to two concurrent chemoradiotherapy regimens. Radiotherapy to the primary tumor was 54 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks.

arms.label: Docetaxel and cisplatin

schema.note: The fluorouracil arm was stopped after a preplanned interim analysis. The cisplatin arm continued.

brief.schema_source: The ACCORD/0201 report states both weekly docetaxel chemoradiotherapy arms and the 54 Gy in 30 fractions radiotherapy.

arms.label: ATG For Cord Blood Transplants
arms.text: If you are undergoing a pre-transplant conditioning regimen prior to undergoing a cord blood transplant, you will receive a drug called ATG to improve your chances of engraftment and decrease your risk of graft versus host disease. You may receive ATG 3 times during your transplant regimen on days -3 through days -1 in addition to your pre-transplant conditioning therapy. Methylprednisolone will also be given during each dose of ATG to help reduce any reactions during infusion.

arms.label: DLI (Donor Leukocyte Infusion)
arms.text: Donor Leukocyte Infusions: You will receive DLI from your original transplant donor. This will be given through a vein , usually in your arm. It will be similar to getting a platelet or blood transfusion. You may require more than one DLI. The decision to give you another infusion will be determined by your condition, relapse status, GVHD and how much DLI you were given before. You may need chemotherapy and/or radiation to improve your disease status prior to additional DLI's.

schema.text: Radiotherapy was administered at a total dose of 39.6 Gy involved-field with 1.8 Gy/fraction 5 times a week.

brief.schema_source: Held et al., HemaSphere 2023 (PMID 37427145). The full text was read.
eligibility: A complete list of exclusion criteria are provided in the protocol in the appendix.

followup.window: Final response was assessed after end of radiotherapy simultaneously with first follow-up in the radiotherapy arm.
First follow-up examination was done 3 months after the restaging after 6 cycles of R-CHOP.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Patients with stage III non-small cell lung cancer, performance status 0-1, and lung V20 below 40% received a single-arm concurrent regimen, then consolidation.

arms.label: Concurrent therapy
arms.text: Cisplatin 75 mg/m2 and pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 every 21 days for three cycles with chest radiotherapy to 66 Gy. The first five patients received cisplatin 60 mg/m2.

arms.label: Consolidation
arms.text: Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 every 21 days for three cycles.

brief.schema_source: The stage III lung trial report states cisplatin and pemetrexed with 66 Gy, followed by three cycles of docetaxel 75 mg/m2.
